verses.zh: 这悖逆、污秽、欺压的城有祸了！
verses.en: Beware to the filthy,[NOTE:1] stained city;the city filled with oppressors![NOTE:2]
notes: The present translation assumes מֹרְאָה (morʾah) is derived from רֹאִי (roʾi, “excrement”; see Jastrow 1436 s.v. רֳאִי). The following participle, “stained,” supports this interpretation (cf. NEB “filthy and foul”; NRSV “soiled, defiled”). Another option is to derive the form from מָרָה (marah, “to rebel”); in this case the term should be translated “rebellious” (cf. NASB, NIV “rebellious and defiled”). This idea is supported by v. 2. For discussion of the two options, see HALOT 630 s.v. I מרא and J. J. M. Roberts, Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah (OTL), 206.
The following verses show that Jerusalem, personified as a woman (“she”), is the referent.
verses.commentary:
3:1 "Woe" This INTERJECTION referred to Nineveh in Nah. 3:4 (cf. Zeph. 2:12-13) but here,
shockingly, to Jerusalem (specifically stated in Zeph. 3:14). This literary technique of mentioning God's judgment on
other nations first (cf. Amos 1:3-2:16) and then on His own people (cf Amos 3:1-6:13) is clearly seen in Amos.

Notice how she is characterized in Zeph. 3:2-5,5e,7e; Hab. 1:3-4.

- rebellious, Zeph. 3:1a ‒ BDB 598, KB 632, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Jer. 4:17; 5:23; 6:28

- defiled, Zeph. 3:1a ‒ BDB 146 II, KB 169, Niphal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Ezek. 23:30

- the tyrannical city, Zeph. 3:1b ‒ BDB 413, KB 416, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, literally"oppressing,"
cf. Jer. 6:6; 22:17

- heeded no voice, Zeph. 3:2a ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT, cf. Jer. 7:23-28

- accepted no instruction, Zeph. 3:2b ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal PERFECT, cf. Jer. 2:30; 5:3; 32:33; 35:13

- did not trust in the Lord, Zeph. 3:2c ‒ BDB 105, KB 120, Qal PERFECT; for the positive usage
of the VERB see 2 Kgs. 18:5; 19:10; 1 Chr. 5:20; Isa. 26:3-4; Jer. 17:7

- did not draw near to her God, Zeph. 3:2d ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, Qal PERFECT, this denotes
worship, cf. 1 Sam. 14:36; Isa. 48:16; Ezek. 44:15

- her leaders (all corrupt)

- her princes are roaring lions

- her judges are wolves at evening, cf. Ezek. 22:27

- her prophets are reckless and treacherous, cf. Jer. 23:32

- her priests have profaned the temple and done violence to the law, cf. Jer. 2:8; Ezek. 22:26

- knows no shame, Zeph. 3:5e, cf. Isa. 42:17; Jer. 2:26; 3:25

- eager to corrupt (two Hiphil PERFECTS) all their deeds, Zeph. 3:7e ‒ a person's repeated choices
and actions reveal the heart

Oh my, what a terrible list of the characteristics of YHWH's people!

Notice numbers 4-7 are all NEGATED PERFECTS, which denotes a settled attitude of defiance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM

verses.zh: 她不听从命令，不领受训诲，不倚靠耶和华，不亲近她的　神。
verses.en: She is disobedient;[NOTE:1] she has refused correction.[NOTE:2] She does not trust the Lord;she has not sought the advice of[NOTE:3] her God.
notes: Heb “she has not listened to a voice.” Refusing to listen is equated with disobedience.
Heb “she has not received correction.” The Hebrew phrase, when negated, refers elsewhere to rejecting verbal advice (Jer 17:23; 32:33; 35:13) and refusing to learn from experience (Jer 2:30; 5:3).
Heb “draw near to.” The translation assumes that the expression “draw near to” refers to seeking God’s will (see 1 Sam 14:36).
verses.commentary:
3:2 "She" The feminine form of the NEGATED VERB reflects the Holy City of YHWH as a fallen,
disobedient, and idolatrous woman (cf. Ezekiel 8; 21; 23).

verses.zh: 她中间的首领是咆哮的狮子；她的审判官是晚上的豺狼，一点食物也不留到早晨。
verses.en: Her princes[NOTE:1] are as fierce as roaring lions;[NOTE:2] her rulers[NOTE:3] are as hungry as wolves in the desert,[NOTE:4] who completely devour their prey by morning.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “officials.”
Heb “her princes in her midst are roaring lions.” The metaphor has been translated as a simile (“as fierce as”) for clarity.
Traditionally “judges.”

Heb “her judges [are] wolves of the evening,” that is, wolves that prowl at night. The translation assumes an emendation to עֲרָבָה (ʿaravah, “desert”). For a discussion of this and other options, see Adele Berlin, Zephaniah (AB 25A), 128. The metaphor has been translated as a simile (“as hungry as”) for clarity.

Heb “they do not gnaw [a bone] at morning.” The precise meaning of the line is unclear. The statement may mean these wolves devour their prey so completely that not even a bone is left to gnaw by the time morning arrives. For a discussion of this and other options, see Adele Berlin, Zephaniah (AB 25A), 129.
verses.commentary:
3:3-4 The leadership of God's people were often condemned by the prophets for their greedy, godless exercise
of power (cf. Isa. 56:9-12; Jer. 5:30-31; 6:13-14; 8:8-12; 14:13-18; 22:1-30; 23:1-40; 26:12-15; 28:1-17; 36:30-31; Ezek.
13:1-23; 22:23-31; Micah 3:1-12; 7:3). As the leadership goes, so go the people!

verses.zh: 她的先知是虚浮诡诈的人；她的祭司亵渎圣所，强解律法。
verses.en: Her prophets are proud;[NOTE:1] they are deceitful men.Her priests have defiled what is holy;[NOTE:2] they have broken God’s laws.[NOTE:3]
notes: Applied to prophets, the word פֹּחֲזִים (pokhazim, “proud”) probably refers to their audacity in passing off their own words as genuine prophecies from the Lord (see Jer 23:32).
These priests defiled what is holy by not observing the proper distinctions between what is ritually clean and unclean (see Ezek 22:26). tn Or “defiled the temple.”
Heb “they treated [the] law violently.”

verses.zh: 耶和华在她中间是公义的，断不做非义的事，每早晨显明他的公义，无日不然；只是不义的人不知羞耻。
verses.en: The just Lord resides[NOTE:1] within her;he commits no unjust acts.[NOTE:2] Every morning he reveals[NOTE:3] his justice.At dawn he appears without fail.[NOTE:4] Yet the unjust know no shame.
notes: The word “resides” is supplied for clarification.
Or “he does no injustice.”
Heb “gives”; or “dispenses.”

Heb “at the light he is not missing.” Note that NASB (which capitalizes pronouns referring to Deity) has divided the lines differently: “Every morning He brings His justice to light; // He does not fail.”
verses.commentary:
3:5 Notice how the Lord (i.e., YHWH) characterizes His future relationship with Jerusalem.

- He is righteousness within her.

- He will do no injustice.

- Every morning He bring His justice to light.

- He does not fail.

The "New Jerusalem" will reflect His character (cf. Revelation 21-22; the new abode of the redeemed people
of God, Jew and Gentile (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13); the promise of Gen. 3:15 is fulfilled at last).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "But the unjust knows no shame" This must refer to Zeph. 3:2-4. It seems out of place in 3:5, as does 3:7e.

verses.zh: 我―耶和华已经除灭列国的民；他们的城楼毁坏。我使他们的街道荒凉，以致无人经过；他们的城邑毁灭，以致无人，也无居民。
verses.en: “I destroyed[NOTE:1] nations;their walled cities[NOTE:2] are in ruins.I turned their streets into ruins;no one passes through them.Their cities are desolate;[NOTE:3] no one lives there.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “cut off.”
Heb “corner towers”; NEB, NRSV “battlements.”
This Hebrew verb (צָדָה, tsadah) occurs only here in the OT, but its meaning is established from the context and from an Aramaic cognate.
Heb “so that there is no man, without inhabitant.”
verses.commentary:
3:6 Because Jerusalem has "no shame" (Zeph. 3:5), YHWH will bring judgment (3:6) on a universal scale
(cf. Zeph. 1:2-18).

The purpose of this judgment (cf. Zeph. 1:2-6,7-13,14-18) is a universal redemption brought about by
Israel's Judean Messiah (Zeph. 3:7d).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CITIES (the two cities in Isaiah)

verses.zh: 我说：你只要敬畏我，领受训诲；如此，你的住处不致照我所拟定的除灭。只是你们从早起来就在一切事上败坏自己。
verses.en: I thought,[NOTE:1] ‘Certainly you will respect[NOTE:2] me!Now you will accept correction!’If she had done so, her home[NOTE:3] would not be destroyed[NOTE:4] by all the punishments I have threatened.[NOTE:5] But they eagerly sinnedin everything they did.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “said.”

Or “fear.” The second person verb form (“you will respect”) is feminine singular, indicating that personified Jerusalem is addressed. sn God’s judgment of the nations (v. 6) was an object lesson for Israel’s benefit.
Or “dwelling place.”
Heb “cut off.”
Heb “all which I have punished her.” The precise meaning of this statement and its relationship to what precedes are unclear.
Heb “But they got up early, they made corrupt all their actions.” The phrase “they got up early” probably refers to their eagerness to engage in sinful activities.
verses.commentary:
3:7 His judgment is for a redemptive purpose (Zeph. 3:7).

- surely you (FEMININE, i.e., Jerusalem) will revere Me, cf. Zeph. 3:9-10 (opposite of 3:2)

- surely you (FEMININE, i.e., Jerusalem) will accept instruction (opposite of 3:2)

- surely you (FEMININE) will be secure

- surely His purposes in "her" (Jerusalem) will be fulfilled

There is coming a new day of fellowship with God. His people, all people, will return to Him. This was
the purpose/goal of creation!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

verses.zh: 耶和华说：你们要等候我，直到我兴起掳掠的日子；因为我已定意招聚列国，聚集列邦，将我的恼怒―就是我的烈怒都倾在她们身上。我的忿怒如火，必烧灭全地。
verses.en: Therefore you must wait patiently[NOTE:1] for me,” says the Lord,“for the day when I attack and take plunder.[NOTE:2] I have decided[NOTE:3] to gather nations togetherand assemble kingdoms,so I can pour out my fury on them—all my raging anger.For[NOTE:4] the whole earth will be consumedby my fiery anger.
notes: The second person verb form (“you must wait patiently”) is masculine plural, indicating that a group is being addressed. Perhaps the humble individuals addressed earlier (see 2:3) are in view. Because of Jerusalem’s sin, they must patiently wait for judgment to pass before their vindication arrives.

Heb “when I arise for plunder.” The present translation takes עַד (ʿad) as “plunder.” Some, following the LXX, repoint the term עֵד (ʿed) and translate, “as a witness” (cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV). In this case the Lord uses a legal metaphor to picture himself as testifying against his enemies. Adele Berlin takes לְעַד (leʿad) in a temporal sense (“forever”) and translates “once and for all” (Zephaniah [AB 25A], 133).
Heb “for my decision is.”
Or “certainly.”
verses.commentary:
3:8 It is interesting to note that Zeph. 3:8 is the only verse in the Hebrew Bible that contains all twenty-two
Hebrew consonants. (Now you are ready for Bible trivia!)

▣ "You" This is MASCULINE, possibly the faithful survivors of Zeph. 2:10 (i.e., "remnant").

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

▣ "wait for Me" This is a Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 314, KB 313, cf. Hab. 2:3).
It is an idiom for trusting (i.e., "endure, expect, hope," NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 129-130) God to act in an appropriate way
at an appropriate time. God will set everything right in His own time and in His own way. His ways are not always clear
to fallen humans (cf. Isa. 55:9-11).

"Waiting" for God is an act of faith in His word (cf. Isa. 8:17; 25:9; 30:18; 64:4; Hab. 2:3).

The NASB Study Bible footnote sees this as a sarcastic statement, affirming Judah's unwillingness to
repent, p. 1324 (also Tyndale OT Commentaries, p. 114).

▣ "the day" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY and
SPECIAL TOPIC: DAY OF THE LORD (NT).

▣

NASB (1970)
"when I rise up to the prey" (different from my text)

NKJV, NET
"I rise up for plunder"

NASB (1995), NRSV, LXX, Peshitta
"when I rise as a witness"

TEV
"when I rise to accuse the nations"

NJB, JPSOA
"when I rise as accuser"

REB
"when I stand up to accuse you"

The MT has דע (BDB 729), which can be pointed

(i.e., vowel points) as

- plunder

- witness

- forever (PREPOSITION plus root)

The UBS Text Project, p. 382, gives option 1 a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

▣ "All My burning anger. . .the fire of My zeal" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ "My decision is to gather nations" Notice the series of INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS

- to the prey ‒ the JPSOA emends this to "when I arise as an accuser"

- to gather, cf. Ezek. 22:19,20

- to assemble

- to pour out

All speak of YHWH's judgment at the appropriate time and in the appropriate way.

▣ Notice the number of PRONOUNS in English denoting YHWH's personal action.

- wait for Me

- I rise up

- My decision

- My indignation

- My burning anger

- My zeal (see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 937-939)

This Divine activity has a redemptive purpose (cf. Zeph. 3:9; 2:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 那时，我必使万民用清洁的言语好求告我―耶和华的名，同心合意地事奉我。
verses.en: Know for sure that I will then enablethe nations to give me acceptable praise.[NOTE:1] All of them will invoke the Lord’s name when they pray[NOTE:2] and will worship him in unison.[NOTE:3]
notes: I will then enable the nations to give me acceptable praise. This apparently refers to a time when the nations will reject their false idol-gods and offer genuine praise to the one true God.tn Heb “Certainly [or perhaps, “For”] then I will restore to the nations a pure lip.”
Heb “so that all of them will call on the name of the Lord.”
Heb “so that [they] will serve him [with] one shoulder.”
verses.commentary:
3:9-10 These verses speak of a universal worship of YHWH (while Zeph. 3:11-13 refers to His covenant
people, see Contextual Insights).

He gives to the peoples purified lips, i.e., examples

- Egypt ‒ Isa. 19:18

- "those far away" ‒ Isa. 57:19

- "among all the wise men of the nations" ‒ Jer. 10:6-7

- "among the nations" ‒ Mal. 1:11

If YHWH is the one, true, creator, then He must also be the one, true redeemer! A universal God demands
universal worship. Israel was a means to an end (i.e., the gospel is for all humans, Matt. 28:19-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8)!

Notice it is God who must "give" (lit. "change"). This is "the new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 (cf. Ezek.
36:22-38) based on God's actions and not human performance (i.e., Mosaic Covenant, cf. Leviticus 26: Deuteronomy 28-30).
But remember, He acts on our behalf so that we can be holy (cf. Matt. 5:48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

NASB
"I will give"

NKJV
"I will restore"

NRSV, TEV, LXX
"I will change"

NJB
"I will purge"

JPSOA
"I will make"

"I will restore"

NET
"I will enable"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 245, KB 253, Qal IMPERFECT),
which basically means "to turn" or "to overturn." KB suggests "restore." Notice the two theological questions.

- YHWH takes the initiative (FIRST PERSON SINGULAR); this is in line with Jer. 31:31-34 (i.e., the
new covenant, cf. Ezek. 36:22-36), but is there a mandated human response?

- Does YHWH "purge" pagan speech (i.e., the nations) or "restore" (i.e., His covenant people); see my bias at Contextual Insights.

▣ "all of them may call on the name of the Lord" This terminology implies an
altar, a sacrifice, and the presence of the Lord. This is not just the speaking of a name (cf. Matt. 7:21-23) but an act of worship
from the heart (cf. Deut. 10:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME (Isa. 12:4)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE NAME OF THE LORD (NT)

▣ "To serve Him shoulder to shoulder" This is a Hebrew idiom for unity (i.e., one burden, two carriers).

verses.zh: 祈祷我的，就是我所分散的民（原文是女子；下同），必从古实河外来，给我献供物。
verses.en: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,[NOTE:1] those who pray to me, my dispersed people,[NOTE:2]will bring me tribute.
notes: Or “Nubia”; Heb “Cush.” “Cush” is traditionally assumed to refer to the region south of Egypt, i.e., Nubia or northern Sudan, referred to as “Ethiopia” by classical authors (not the more recent Abyssinia).

It is not certain if those who pray to me refers to the converted nations or to God’s exiled covenant people.tn Heb “those who pray to me, the daughter of my dispersed ones.” The meaning of the phrase is unclear. For a discussion of various options see Adele Berlin, Zephaniah (AB 25A), 134-35.
verses.commentary:
3:10 Some see this as referring only to dispersed, exiled Israel and Judah (cf. Zeph. 3:11-13) but the context
of universal judgment (i.e., Zeph. 1:2-3,18; 2:3b,11) implies a universal opportunity for inclusion (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9;
42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-8; 60:1-3; 66:23; Mic. 4:1-4; Mal. 1:11).

There are three texts in Isaiah that speak specifically of the conversion of Ethiopia/Egypt ‒ Isa. 18:7;
19:18-25; 45:14.

3:10b

NASB
"My worshipers, My dispersed ones"

NKJV
"My worshipers, The daughter of My dispersed ones"

NRSV
"my supplicants, my scattered ones"

TEV
"my scattered people"

NJB
"My suppliants"

The JPSOA translates this line as no standard English translation.

"Shall bring offerings to Me in Fair Puzai"

The Jewish Study Bible offers three suggestions (p. 1241).

- "Fair scattered (i.e., Israel in exile), shall bring my offerings"

- "Fair Puzai (i.e., a faraway nation) shall bring my offering" (so too, AB, pp. 126, 135)

- "Fair scattered (i.e., Israel in exile), they (i.e., the nations) shall bring as my offering" (cf. Isa. 66:20)

verses.zh: 当那日，你必不因你一切得罪我的事自觉羞愧；因为那时我必从你中间除掉矜夸高傲之辈，你也不再于我的圣山狂傲。
verses.en: In that day you[NOTE:1] will not be ashamed of all your rebelliousness against me,[NOTE:2] for then I will remove from your midst those who proudly boast,[NOTE:3] and you will never again be arrogant on my holy hill.
notes: The second person verbs and pronouns are feminine singular, indicating that personified Jerusalem is addressed here.
Heb “In that day you will not be ashamed because of all your actions, [in] which you rebelled against me.”
Heb “the arrogant ones of your pride.”
verses.commentary:
3:11 "you" This is FEMININE SINGULAR and refers to Jerusalem (cf. Zeph. 3:2).

▣ YHWH will remove the wicked people from His people.

- the ones who rebel

- the proud ones

- the exulting ones

- the haughty ones (see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 797-799)

It is hard for modern western people to acknowledge that sin and rebellion against God results in death and
separation. The right and dignity of the individual in western thought has eclipsed the biblical view of God's righteous judgment.
Some humans are going to die!

A helpful book on this is John W. Wenham, The Goodness of God.

▣ "from your midst" There is a play on this word (BDB 899) in Zephaniah 3.

- Zeph. 3:1 ‒ Judah's corrupt leaders are in her midst

- Zeph. 3:5 ‒ YHWH is in her midst

- Zeph. 3:11 ‒ YHWH removes "the proud, exulting, haughty ones" from their midst

- Zeph. 3:12 ‒ YHWH leaves a humble lowly people in His midst

- Zeph. 3:15 ‒ YHWH, the King of Israel, is in her midst!

verses.zh: 我却要在你中间留下困苦贫寒的民；他们必投靠我―耶和华的名。
verses.en: I will leave in your midst a humble and meek group of people,[NOTE:1] and they will find safety in the Lord’s presence.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “needy and poor people.” The terms often refer to a socioeconomic group, but here they may refer to those who are humble in a spiritual sense.

Heb “and they will take refuge in the name of the Lord.” sn Safety in the Lord’s presence. From the time the Lord introduced his special covenant name (Yahweh) to Moses, it served as a reminder of his protective presence as Israel’s faithful deliverer.
verses.commentary:
3:12-13 The people of YHWH will be characterized as

- humble (in a spiritual sense, cf. Zeph. 2:3)

- lowly

- those who take refuge in the name of the Lord

- do no wrong

- tell no lies, cf. Zech. 8:3,16

- have no deceitful tongue

God is their shepherd (i.e., Zeph. 3:13e,f). This is the result of the repentance of Zeph. 2:3. They are now secure
in their land (i.e., "no one to make them tremble or be afraid," cf. Jer. 30:10; 46:27; Ezek. 34:28; 39:26; Mic. 4:4)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE IN THE OT

verses.zh: 以色列所剩下的人必不作罪孽，不说谎言，口中也没有诡诈的舌头；而且吃喝躺卧，无人惊吓。
verses.en: The Israelites who remain[NOTE:1] will not act deceitfully.They will not lie,and a deceitful tongue will not be found in their mouths.Indeed, they will graze peacefully like sheep[NOTE:2] and lie down;no one will terrify them.”
notes: Or “the remnant of Israel.”
The words “peacefully like sheep” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 锡安的民哪，应当歌唱！以色列啊，应当欢呼！耶路撒冷的民哪，应当满心欢喜快乐！
verses.en: Shout for joy, Daughter Zion![NOTE:1] Shout out, Israel!Be happy and boast with all your heart, Daughter Jerusalem!
notes: This phrase is used as an epithet for the city and the nation. “Daughter” may seem extraneous in English but consciously joins the various epithets and metaphors of Israel and Jerusalem as a woman, a device used to evoke sympathy from the reader.
verses.commentary:
3:14 There is a series of IMPERATIVES.

- shout for joy ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal

- shout in triumph ‒ BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil

- rejoice ‒ BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal

- exult with all your heart ‒ BDB 759, KB 831, Qal

Notice "Zion," "Israel" and "daughter of Jerusalem" are parallel.

The strophe, Zeph. 3:14-20, is a psalm of joy. It is a contrast to the universal judgment of the rest of
the book. The judgment of "that day" will bring about "a new day" (cf. Zeph. 3:9-10)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (THE NAME)

verses.zh: 耶和华已经除去你的刑罚，赶出你的仇敌。以色列的王―耶和华在你中间；你必不再惧怕灾祸。
verses.en: The Lord has removed the judgment against you;[NOTE:1] he has turned back your enemy.Israel’s king, the Lord, is in your midst!You no longer need to fear disaster.
notes: Heb “your judgments,” that is, “the judgments directed against you.” The translation reflects the implications of the parallelism.
verses.commentary:
3:15 The first two VERBS, "taken away" and "cleared away" are both
FIRST PERSON PERFECTS. They refer to future actions of YHWH that have not yet happened, but the
assurance that they will caused the author to state them as completed acts (i.e., PROPHETIC PERFECT;
note Isa. 55:9-11).

▣ "The King of Israel, the Lord" YHWH is the true King of His covenant people;
the earthly king was merely His representative (cf. 1 Sam. 8:5-7). The rabbis call Him "the King of the Universe"!

Notice the two names for God that appear in Zeph. 3:17.

- The Lord (YHWH) your God (Elohim)

- A victorious warrior ‒ this is Holy War terminology for YHWH as the Divine Warrior, cf. Exod. 15:3; Deut. 1:30; Jos. 5:13-15;
1 Chr. 20:29; Ps. 24:8; Isa. 42:13; 59:17. The title "Lord of Hosts" reflects this same imagery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS

▣ "is in your midst" This is the greatest promise (see note at Zeph. 3:11)! YHWH was with Moses.
YHWH was in the midst of Israel. This Divine-human fellowship is the purpose of creation (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).
Humans were created for fellowship. Sin has separated us from our Creator. God's promises in Isaiah 7; 9; and 11
is that One is coming Who is "Emmanuel" (i.e., God with us).

The Bible starts with God and mankind in fellowship in a garden (i.e., Genesis 1-2) and the Bible ends
with God and mankind in fellowship in a garden (Revelation 21-22).

His people will not need an earthly king because the Divine King is with them! One wonders how this
relates to 1 Cor. 15:25-28.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你的　神是施行拯救、大有能力的主。他在你中间必因你欢欣喜乐，默然爱你，且因你喜乐而欢呼。
verses.en: The Lord your God is in your midst;he is a warrior who can deliver.He takes great delight in you;[NOTE:1] he renews you by his love;[NOTE:2] he shouts for joy over you.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he rejoices over you with jubilation.” The term שִׂמְכָּה (simkah) can mean joy or the expression of joy. In light of the last line of the verse, this line may imply shouts of joy.

The MT reads, “he remains silent in his love,” a Hiphil form of the stative verb חָרַשׁ (kharash, “to be silent, deaf”). But this does not make sense in light of the expressions of joy in the preceding and following lines. All other cases of the Hiphil of this verb mean to act silently, maintain silence, or the like. This is normal for stative verbs in the Hiphil, where they often mean to behave with the attribute expressed by the root. Some commentators appeal to Job 11:3 as a possible causative use, “Should your boasting silence men?” But in fact the verse should be understood as “should men remain silent at your boasts?” The LXX reads “he will renew you with his love,” implying יְחַדֵּשׁ (yekhaddesh), a Piel from the root חָדַשׁ (khadash, “to make new, restore”). This assumes the confusion of ד (dalet) and ר (resh) in the MT. The direct object “you” should be understood either through ellipsis or by possible haplography, with the כ (kaf) having been dropped before the similar looking ב (bet) beginning the next word. Renewal is a fitting concept after judgment (cf. Lam 5:21).
Heb “he rejoices over you with a shout of joy.”
verses.commentary:
3:17 This verse repeats the great promise of Zeph. 3:15 ("in your midst"; see full note at Zeph. 3:11) and
expresses God's joy (cf. Isa. 65:19) at the renewal of fellowship with His human creation.

- He will exult over you with joy (cf. Deut. 30:9; Isa. 62:5; 65:19; Jer. 32:41).

- He will renew you in His love (following the LXX, Peshitta; the MT has "be silent"; the difference is the Hebrew
"r" and "d" confusion).

- He will rejoice over you with shout of joy.

verses.zh: 那些属你、为无大会愁烦、因你担当羞辱的，我必聚集他们。
verses.en: “As for those who grieve because they cannot attend the festivals—I took them away from you;they became tribute and were a source of shame to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The ones grieving from an assembly I gathered from you they were, tribute upon her, a reproach.” Any translation of this difficult verse must be provisional at best. The present translation assumes three things: (1) The preposition מִן (min) prefixed to “assembly” is causal (the individuals are sorrowing because of the assemblies or festivals they are no longer able to hold). (2) מַשְׂאֵת (masʾet) means “tribute” and refers to the exiled people being treated as the spoils of warfare (see R. D. Patterson, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah [WEC], 385-86). (3) The third feminine singular suffix refers to personified Jerusalem, which is addressed earlier in the verse (the pronominal suffix in “from you” is second feminine singular). For other interpretive options see Adele Berlin, Zephaniah (AB 25A), 146.
verses.commentary:
3:18-20 This verse is uncertain in Hebrew (see JPSOA's footnote) but seems to address the exiled people
of God who, one day, will be able to attend the feast days (cf. Exodus 23; Leviticus 23) in Jerusalem, in the temple again!

These verses seem to address restored, repentant Israel/Judah. The Gentiles (cf. Zeph. 3:20) will
recognize YHWH as Israel's God. They will praise Him (cf. Jer. 3:17,19; 4:2; 16:19; 33:9). He has a universal redemptive
purpose in her!

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Who is "the rebellious" city of Zeph. 3:1?

- List the reasons why she is called rebellious.

- How is Zeph. 3:7 so different from 3:1-6?

- What does the VERB "wait" mean?

- For what two purposes will YHWH gather the nations?

- How is Zeph. 3:8 like Zephaniah, chapter 1?

- Why is Zeph. 3:9-10 so theologically significant?

- Does Zeph. 3:15 speak of a Messianic reign (i.e., 1,000 years) or an eternal reign (cf. Dan. 7:13)?

verses.zh: 那时，我必罚办一切苦待你的人，又拯救你瘸腿的，聚集你被赶出的。那些在全地受羞辱的，我必使他们得称赞，有名声。
verses.en: Look, at that time I will deal with those who mistreated you.I will rescue the lame sheep[NOTE:1] and gather together the scattered sheep.I will take away their humiliationand make the whole earth admire and respect them.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “sheep” is supplied for clarification. As in Mic 4:6-7, the exiles are here pictured as injured and scattered sheep whom the divine shepherd rescues from danger.
Heb “I will make them into praise and a name, in all the earth, their shame.” The present translation assumes that “their shame” specifies “them” and that “name” stands here for a good reputation.

verses.zh: 那时，我必领你们进来，聚集你们；我使你们被掳之人归回的时候，就必使你们在地上的万民中有名声，得称赞。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: At that time I will lead you—at the time I gather you together.[NOTE:1] Be sure of this![NOTE:2] I will make all the nations of the earth respect and admire you[NOTE:3] when you see me restore you,”[NOTE:4] says the Lord.
notes: In this line the second person pronoun is masculine plural, indicating that the exiles are addressed.
Or “for.”
Heb “I will make you into a name and praise among all the peoples of the earth.” Here the word “name” carries the nuance of “good reputation.”
Heb “when I restore your fortunes to your eyes.” See the note on the phrase “restore them” in 2:7.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

I must admit that my theological bias shows brightly in Zephaniah 2-3. I view all texts through the Great
Commission (i.e., Matt. 28:19-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8). It is difficult to know if these chapters are using universal themes
as hyperbole or emphasizing God's universal redemption.

It is quite possible that this context refers only to repentant, restored Israel/Judah. But there are so many
OT texts about God's love for all humans that I consciously err on this side of universal hope. I believe in a universal offer
but a divine mandate for repentance and faith for inclusion. I do not believe in universalism, but I do believe in a universal
offer! Oh, how I love John 1:12; 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14!
